newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market rate up 70 bps at 11.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market rate up 70 bps at 11.8 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate ended 70 basis points higher at 11.8 percent on Tuesday, although weaker demand caused lenders to cut call money back by 50 basis points.
Total trade was put by dealers at a lower 48 million kuna, leaving a surplus of over 30 million in supply.
Interbank call money at a weighted 10.6 percent accounted for most of the day's 36 million kuna fresh borrowings. Term deals were struck at an unchanged 14-16 percent.
Insurers charged betwen nine percent for one-week funds and 18 percent -- their record in weeks -- for one-month kuna.
The central bank calculated the kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.9768 against the dollar and 3.5785 to the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
